title: Persist fixed-expiry MCP grants and atomically rotate opaque host tokens
description:
## Intent

Make a connection's deadline, ownership and revocation authoritative in the private grant service. This task uses provider fixtures and can land before the actual Cognito integration.

## Steps

1. Extend amplify/functions/mcp-oauth/{grants,store,handler}.py and the site KMS/Dynamo provisioning in amplify/mcp-oauth/resource.ts. Separate pending transaction, grant, and spent refresh records using distinct key namespaces in the existing per-site table. A grant has immutable site/Account, verified identity kind and subject, client, resource, registered redirect, approval time and hard expiry, plus state, version and token hashes. The code is single use, capped at five minutes and at the grant deadline. An access token expires at the earlier of 15 minutes, the grant deadline and any downstream credential it depends on.
2. Fix hard expiry once, min(approval + seven days, verified original upstream deadline). Preserve the short path using verified browser token/session expiry. Never extend the fixed deadline on refresh. Use trusted server time. Read expiry on every verify/exchange/refresh, including before TTL cleanup. Hash opaque MCP secrets at rest and envelope-encrypt upstream credentials, with site/grant encryption context.
3. Remove the 128-refresh cap, which cannot sustain seven days of 15-minute access. Put a spent-token hash record keyed by grant and hash with expiry at the hard deadline. Atomically conditionally update the grant version and write the spent record via DynamoDB TransactWriteItems. One active refresh per grant. Replace the current access hash in the same atomic commit so its previous token fails immediately. Check client, resource and applicable redirect/PKCE binding before acting on replay. A validated spent refresh revokes that family and leaves no successor usable. A random or wrong-client/site token fails without affecting the valid connection. Serialize revocation and rotation on the same version, return a retryable service failure on storage contention or unavailability rather than reporting an uncommitted revoke.
4. Treat existing short grants as legacy bounded to their original deadline. Invalidate them at renewable enablement and require a new authorization on the same connection. Version records explicitly and verify legacy credentials never become renewable by inference. Keep client registrations and site URL. Deploy dormant support before enabling on a reviewed test site.
5. Retain spent hashes through the deadline, bound request size and abusive refresh frequency, and never record bearer tokens, authorization codes or upstream secrets in logs. Use audit events with stage, outcome and non-secret grant identifier only.

## Gherkin acceptance

Feature: Use a rotating MCP session within a fixed deadline
Scenario: Two refresh calls present the same token
  Given one valid refresh token for an active connection
  When it is submitted concurrently twice
  Then at most one successor is issued
  And detected replay makes every successor unusable

Scenario: A client refreshes throughout a week
  Given a renewable staff connection with a seven-day deadline
  When the client refreshes every fifteen minutes
  Then the connection remains eligible up to the deadline
  And the deadline never moves
  And refresh and tool use fail at the deadline

Scenario: An unrelated client tries a spent token
  Given a spent token belongs to a different client or publication
  When it is presented to the token endpoint
  Then it cannot renew or revoke that grant

## Verification

Extend features_backend/mcp-oauth.feature, the grant and concurrency pytest suites, and the store tests for conditional failures and expiry. Test the transaction against a local DynamoDB fixture or equivalent transaction contract and record that evidence separately from in-memory tests.

comments.text: Draft engine PR #1244 (https://github.com/AnthusAI/Papyrus/pull/1244), feature/PPY-2bc3e8-authenticated-mcp, includes atomic rotation in 60101882. The seven-day simulated rotation regression failed at the previous cap and passes with TTL-bound spent-token hashes. Lead verification: 14 focused Python tests and 13 OAuth/hosting Gherkin scenarios. Live provider renewal and stable HTTPS host proof are separate.
